title: org.projectfile.deploy extension (v1)
description: Standalone contract for the value at the org.projectfile.deploy subtree: what a project needs in order to run well, stated as intent and never as mechanism. Each key is a UNIT, one running part of the project, pointing at a service artifact in org.projectfile.artifacts that already says what runs, what it listens on and what it must be given. No field names a platform: a reader (a compose file generator, a Helm chart generator, a cloud template, a written runbook) translates each intent into its own terms, and a reader that cannot honour an intent MUST fail naming the unit, the field and itself, never drop it silently. How healthy a unit is comes from org.projectfile.health, not from here.

unit.description: One running part of the project.

runs.description: The name of the artifact this unit runs, a key of org.projectfile.artifacts. The artifact owns its image, ports, secrets and settings; the unit repeats none of them.

shape.description: How many copies run, and for how long. `singleton`: at most one at any moment, never two during an update (a database, anything holding a lock on its data). `scalable`: any number of copies serve the same thing, and a new one may start before an old one stops. `per-machine`: one on every machine that runs workloads (a log shipper). `scheduled`: runs to completion on the cadence in `every`, then sleeps. `once`: runs to completion before any unit that needs it starts (a migration).

every.description: The cadence of a `scheduled` unit (`P1D` is daily). Only with `shape: scheduled`, where it is REQUIRED.

at.description: The time of day a `scheduled` unit starts, 24-hour `HH:MM` in the deployment’s time zone. Absent means any time the reader picks.

size.description: A named size class, never cores and bytes. Each class is a CPU and memory ceiling a reader turns into its own limits: `nano` ¼ core and 128 MiB, `micro` ½ core and 256 MiB, `tiny` ½ core and 512 MiB, `small` 1 core and 1 GiB, `medium` 2 cores and 2 GiB, `large` 2 cores and 4 GiB, `xlarge` 4 cores and 8 GiB, `2xlarge` 8 cores and 16 GiB. Absent means the reader’s default class.

keeps.description: What this unit writes that must outlive one run of it, by name. A unit that keeps nothing may lose every byte it wrote on any restart.

offers.description: What this unit serves, and to whom, by name. A port of the artifact that no offer names is reachable by nobody.

needs.description: What this unit needs from the world, by name. A unit with no needs calls nobody, and a reader MAY deny it every outbound connection.

keep.description: One thing a unit keeps: where it lives and what losing it costs. Exactly one of `worth` and `backup`.

at.description: The absolute path inside the running unit where this data lives.

worth.description: A named norm class. `irreplaceable`: lose at most one hour of it, keep a year of copies, keep one copy on another machine, and prove a restore weekly; the same as the explicit `backup` {lose-at-most: PT1H, keep: P1Y, elsewhere: true, prove-restore: P1W}. `rebuildable`: no copies; losing it costs time, not data, and a reader SHOULD still keep it across restarts. `disposable`: it MAY vanish on every restart.

backup.description: The explicit norm, for data no class fits. A reader that schedules copies also alerts when the newest good copy is older than `lose-at-most`.

lose-at-most.description: The most recent writes a failure may lose: the longest gap between two good copies.

keep.description: How long each copy is kept.

elsewhere.description: At least one copy lives on a machine other than the one the unit runs on.

prove-restore.description: How often a copy is restored into scratch space to prove it works. Absent means never proven, which a reader SHOULD warn about.

port.description: The `name` of one of the artifact’s ports.

to.description: The audience. `everyone`: the public internet. `operators`: the people who run the deployment and nobody else (an admin page, a metrics port). `units`: other units of the same deployment only. `peers`: other machines on the internet speaking the same protocol, with no name in front (BitTorrent, Radicle).

at.description: The public name it is served under, usually an expression over deployment values (`${domain}`). Only with `to: everyone` or `to: operators`, and only for a port that `speaks` a protocol with names in it (`http`).

capability.description: What kind of thing is needed, never which product. Open vocabulary; the first set: `relational-database`, `key-value-cache`, `object-store`, `message-queue`, `internet` (may call out at all). `unit:<name>` names another unit of the same deployment.

need.description: One thing a unit needs. A bare capability when the unit learns nothing from it; the object form when the reader must hand the unit how to reach it.

fills.description: Which of the artifact’s `settings` receives each part of what the reader provides, keyed by part (`url`, `host`, `port`, `username`, `password`, `database`). The setting’s own `secret` flag says how the value is delivered.

trust.description: How far the unit is trusted. `exposed`: it handles input from strangers, so a reader isolates it as far as it can. `internal`: it sees only its own deployment. The object form adds the powers it cannot run without, in plain words (`network-admin`, `tun-device`); a reader that cannot grant one MUST fail. Absent means `exposed` with no powers, the secure default.
